purpose: Move the essential-purchasing-power lane from national price context toward directly reported household conditions using March 2026 Census HTOPS measures of food sufficiency, household energy spending, expense difficulty, price stress, and transportation sufficiency.
source_authority: U.S. Census Bureau Household Trends and Outlook Pulse Survey (HTOPS)
official_sample_context: Census reports that the March 2026 detailed tables cover data collected from approximately 136,000 households and include national and smaller-area estimates.

official_direct_burden_lanes.official_table: Food Sufficiency for Households in the Last Seven Days, by Select Characteristics
Household Energy Use and Spending in the Last Two Months, by Select Characteristics
Difficulty Paying Usual Household Expenses in the Last Two Months, by Select Characteristics
Sufficiency of Access to Transportation During the Last Four Weeks, by Select Characteristics
Stress Caused by Price Increases, by Select Characteristics

secondary_weighted_reconstruction_leads.provenance: independent weighted reconstruction of March 2026 HTOPS public-use file using PWEIGHT
secondary_weighted_reconstruction_leads.use_rule: Triangulation only until official Census workbook values are directly preserved. Do not label the 22.48% category food insufficiency; it reflects enough quantity but constrained preferred food access.

secondary_weighted_reconstruction_leads.use_rule: Triangulation only. Secondary presentation contains inconsistent headline wording for broader 'any difficulty' aggregates, so only explicitly defined category combinations may be retained.

secondary_weighted_reconstruction_leads.provenance: independent weighted reconstruction of March 2026 HTOPS public-use file using PWEIGHT
secondary_weighted_reconstruction_leads.use_rule: Self-reported price perception, not an objective price index and not a causal attribution.

secondary_weighted_reconstruction_leads.use_rule: Strong distributional lead showing materially greater reported stress at lower incomes; official-table custody remains required before canonical numeric promotion.

conflicting_secondary_lead.provenance: separate secondary analysis citing U.S. Census HTOPS
conflicting_secondary_lead.reason: The value differs from another PUF-derived presentation's 19.77% significant-difficulty measure and may reflect a different population, category aggregation, denominator, or survey interpretation. Preserve the conflict until the official Census workbook is directly read.

survey_design_guard.comparability_rule: Do not directly compare March 2026 expense-difficulty levels with prior waves that used different recall windows or longitudinal designs without an explicit bridge.

governing_interpretation: These lanes measure directly reported household constraint or service sufficiency and are closer to lived economic burden than CPI alone.
Food insufficiency is not equivalent to lower underlying food demand; it is evidence of unmet or incompletely satisfied need.
Having enough food but not always the kinds wanted may reflect substitution, affordability, availability, preference, or other constraints and must not be collapsed into outright insufficiency.
Difficulty paying usual expenses is not a causal attribution to diesel, freight, utilities, or food by itself.
Household energy spending must remain distinct from electricity commodity rate because delivery charges, usage, geography, fuel choice, and contract structure can differ.
Transportation insufficiency may reflect price, availability, safety, disability, or other reasons; cause-specific fields must be preserved if directly custodied.
Survey redesign and recall-window changes prohibit casual time-series comparisons across incompatible HTOPS/HPS waves.
Secondary weighted reconstructions are useful for locating likely burden gradients but cannot substitute for direct official-table custody when conflicting derived values exist.
